craft_notes: Sthāyin: self-told (svākya — whose happiness to tell is THIS one). Rows: row 3 (happiness→told). Close: told (ucyate — the telling-claim: only this is tellable, echoing v157's secrecy from the other side). Rejected: 'theology' — killed: self-told kept; 'any happiness' — killed: brahman-reality's kept (the qualifier IS the verse).

lines: Agitated by union, shaking, power-penetration's end:
whatever brahman-reality's happiness — self-told, that told.
l4.sanskrit_cite: śaktisaṃgamasaṃkṣubdhaśaktyāveśāvasānikam | yat sukham brahmatattvasya tat sukhaṃ svākyam ucyate

reads_against.argmap: What happiness is truly told? → Only the brahman-reality's happiness, own-told, is the happiness to tell.
c1_essence: Only brahman-reality's happiness, self-told, is told.
reads_against.c1_rasa: adbhuta charged with vīra (wonder armed with intensity)
